about: Shared by apps/test/features/calendar/domain/recurrence_expansion_parity_test.dart (the client's EventOccurrenceExpander) and server/tests/Application.UnitTests/Common/RecurrenceExpanderTests.cs (the server's RecurrenceExpander). Both must produce `expected` for every case, so the calendar and the server agree on which days a series has. All times are local wall-clock (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm): the client evaluates rules on the device's clock, the server on UTC+7, and comparing wall-clock values keeps the check independent of the machine's time zone. Occurrences sit well inside the range and away from any UNTIL, because the two engines may treat the edges of a window differently; edge behaviour is pinned by the server's own tests. A case with `clientGap` is a valid rule the client cannot expand yet: the server must still produce `expected`, and the client test asserts it still produces nothing — so fixing the client turns that test red, as a reminder to delete `clientGap`.
